applies_to: ABB ACH 400 HVAC drives read over Modbus RTU by a Contemporary Controls BASgatewayLX.
summary: Gateway profile for the ABB ACH 400 HVAC drive: 270 objects (249 AI, 21 BI), 62 polled by default. It reads the status word bits, output frequency, current, speed, power, DC bus voltage, fault history and the drive parameter groups. Every object is an input, so the profile monitors the drive but cannot command it.
notes: Built from Contemporary Controls' BASgatewayLX Modbus device profile ABB_ACH_400_Drive_a_LX.CSV; the profile maps the registers in the ACH 400 user's manual Modbus section (https://www.ccontrols.com/support/dp/ACH402_US_04_Web.pdf).
Object instances are the ones this profile assigns when it is loaded into the gateway. A site that edited or rebuilt the profile may use different instances.
Only 62 of the 270 rows are flagged for polling in the profile; the rest are served only after you tick them in the gateway. Their descriptions say "not polled by default".

The CSV has no read/write column: Analog/Binary Inputs are read-only and Analog/Binary Outputs are commandable (priority array), which is how the gateway maps them (access inferred). Descriptions give the Modbus register each object reads.
Some names appear more than once in the profile as published (PID GAIN; PID INTEG TIME; PID DERIV TIME...); they are kept as printed and told apart by instance.

The engineering units in this profile look shifted by one row from about AI 26 on (e.g. SPEED shows amperes, OUTPUT FREQ shows rpm); they are kept as printed, so check units against the ACH 400 manual before trending.

integration.summary: Poll the status bits and actual values for monitoring. The profile has no writable objects, so drive commands need another path (hard-wired I/O or an edited profile).
setup: The BASgatewayLX presents each Modbus device as its own virtual BACnet device on BACnet IP; give it a unique device instance and Modbus address (serial) or IP address (Modbus TCP) when you add it with this profile.
One BASgatewayLX handles up to 100 Modbus devices and 1000 polled points in total, so leave unneeded rows unpolled.
gotchas: The profile is read-only: it has no output objects, so start/stop and speed reference cannot be written through it as published.
Unpolled rows do not appear as BACnet objects until enabled in the gateway's device profile page.
